# Headline statistics (auto-generated by scripts/headline_stats.py)

Do not edit by hand. Re-run the script after any data change.

## 1. Sample

- Raw rows (48 files): 19,821
- After the notebook's cleaning (2010-2025, six valid journal titles): 19,538
- After removing duplicate rows (same DOI and country): 17,291 (2,247 removed)

## 4. Impact metrics by first-author gender

Records with metrics: 17,148 (metrics missing for 0 records). `Citations` is the citation count in the Elsevier/PlumX metrics columns (the column the notebook used for its citation gap).

| metric | mean male | mean female | median male | median female | Mann-Whitney p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Citations | 43.10 | 40.23 | 24.0 | 23.0 | 0.097 |
| Usages | 12.72 | 8.95 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.57 |
| Captures | 72.02 | 69.50 | 41.0 | 41.0 | 0.51 |
| Mentions | 0.34 | 0.39 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.036 |
| Social Media | 250.44 | 204.25 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.64 |
| Citations (Crossref) | 40.39 | 37.62 | 23.0 | 21.0 | 0.15 |
| First Author H-Index | 14.71 | 11.21 | 10.0 | 8.0 | 1.6e-45 |

- Raw gap: male first-authored papers receive **7.13%** more citations on average (43.10 vs 40.23); medians 24 vs 23; Mann-Whitney p = 0.097.

Controlled models (OLS on log(1 + citations), HC1 robust SE; coefficient converted to % difference female vs male):

| model | % difference (female vs male) | 95% CI | p | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 gender only | -2.3% | -6.2 to +1.9 | 0.28 | 17,148 |
| M2 + year, journal, country | +1.9% | -1.3 to +5.3 | 0.25 | 17,148 |
| M3 + first-author h-index | +6.0% | +2.6 to +9.4 | 0.00039 | 17,148 |

Raw citation gap by period:

| period | mean male | mean female | % more for male | Mann-Whitney p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2010-2019 | 53.78 | 51.62 | +4.2% | 0.76 |
| 2020-2025 | 19.57 | 18.68 | +4.8% | 0.98 |
